source_text: Central to the debate is the tension between parental authority and child autonomy: proponents argue that modest empirical benefits—such as a 10-fold reduction in urinary tract infections during infancy and partial protection against heterosexual HIV acquisition in adulthood—outweigh rare risks (estimated at 0.2-0.6% for adverse events), justifying proxy decision-making by guardians in line with cultural or familial values. [1] [2] [6]
